hypothesis: A temporarily unsynchronized eight-asset return panel is a narrowly identifiable concurrent source-refresh condition and should trigger the existing one-second degraded retry without weakening strict failures for persistent source, schema, or identity defects.
decision: Retain the exact retry classification. The production monitor died on this condition, the same authenticated source subsequently converged, the pre-repair regression failed, 6910 non-network tests passed after repair, and the restarted authority-none monitor published across three recurring cycles. No live backend, strategy, exit, sizing, leverage, or risk change is supported or required by this repair.
falsifier: Reject or revise the classification if the same stable authenticated prefix remains unsynchronized, repeated retries produce stale output without visible degradation, an unrelated ValueError is suppressed, or the monitor terminates on another transient instance.
limitations: Three post-repair publications do not establish indefinite process reliability.
A permanent source mismatch will remain visible as repeated degraded cycles and stale report age rather than being reinterpreted as a valid panel.
The report-only monitor still relies on external process and freshness supervision.
This reliability repair provides no evidence about strategy profitability.
